51.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
51.solution: For the cell reaction \(n = 2\) electrons are transferred. Using \(\Delta G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}\):\n\(-386000 = -2 \times 96500 \times E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}\)\n\(E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = \dfrac{-386000}{-2 \times 96500} = 2.00\ \text{V}\)

52.solution: A bcc unit cell has a packing efficiency of 68%, so the volume actually occupied by the particles is \(0.34\) of the unit-cell volume (since each bcc cell effectively contains 2 atoms and the fraction per the standard relation is 0.34 of the cell volume). With unit-cell volume \(= 8.2 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^{3}\):\n\(V_{\text{particle}} = 0.34 \times 8.2 \times 10^{-23} = 2.788 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^{3}\)
52.note: Stem garbled: cell volume reads '.2' but the intended value is 8.2e-23 cm^3 (only value consistent with the keyed option C).

53.solution: When an aryl halide reacts with an alkyl halide in the presence of sodium metal in dry ether, the coupling gives a substituted aromatic (alkylbenzene). This is the Wurtz-Fittig reaction.
53.note: Options are garbled: the intended correct answer is the WURTZ-FITTIG reaction (aryl halide + alkyl halide + Na/dry ether). Option B 'Wurtzilite' is the keyed option meant to represent Wurtz-Fittig (Wurtzilite is actually a mineral). 'Fitting'=Fittig (aryl+aryl only), 'Wirtz'=Wurtz (alkyl+alkyl only), Finkelstein is halide exchange. Source-paper option typo.

54.solution: Schiff's reagent (decolourised fuchsin) restores a pink/magenta colour with aldehydes in the cold. Among the options only the aldehyde gives the test. 'Propanil' here is the source paper's spelling of propanal (an aldehyde), so it gives the pink colour.
54.note: Option C 'Propanil' is a source-paper misspelling of propanal (the aldehyde); propanol, propanone (ketone) and propanoic acid do not give the Schiff's test.

55.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
55.solution:
For isothermal reversible compression of an ideal gas:
\(W = -2.303\,nRT\log_{10}\dfrac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}\)
\(W = -2.303 	imes 1 	imes 8.314 	imes 300 	imes \log_{10}\dfrac{6}{12}\)
\(= -5744 	imes \log_{10}(0.5) = +5744 	imes 0.3010 = 1729\ 	ext{J} = 1.729\ 	ext{kJ}\)
The work is positive (work done on the gas during compression).

56.note: Stem garbled: edge length reads '.0' but the intended value is 4.0e-8 cm (only value consistent with keyed option B).

57.subtopic: Complex Types, Homoleptic, Heteroleptic, Cationic, Anionic, Neutral
57.solution: Tetraamminedibromoplatinum(IV) bromide is written \([Pt(NH_{3})_{4}Br_{2}]Br_{2}\); it contains the complex cation \([Pt(NH_{3})_{4}Br_{2}]^{2+}\) together with bromide anions. The other options are a single cationic complex ion, a neutral complex, and a complex anion respectively.
57.note: Textbook-keyed answer (C). Strictly [Pt(NH3)4Br2]Br2 has a complex cation and a SIMPLE bromide anion (not a complex anion), but among the four options C is the only one that contains a complex ion paired with a counter-ion; it is the intended MHT-CET answer.

58.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
58.solution: Rate \(= k[A]^{x}\). Increasing \([A]\) tenfold multiplies the rate by \(10^{x}\). Given the rate increases 100 times: \(10^{x} = 100 \Rightarrow x = 2\). Order \(= 2\).

59.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
59.solution: Terbium (Tb, Z = 65) has the configuration \([Xe]4f^{9}6s^{2}\). On forming \(Tb^{4+}\) it loses 4 electrons to give a half-filled, stable \(4f^{7}\) configuration. Hence Tb exhibits the +4 state with an \(f^{7}\) configuration.

60.solution: A salt that turns red litmus blue gives a basic solution. KCN is the salt of a strong base (KOH) and a weak acid (HCN); it hydrolyses to give a basic solution. NaNO3, NaCl and KCl are salts of strong acid and strong base and are neutral.

61.subtopic: Real Gases, Dalton's Law and KTG
61.solution: Moles: \(n_{N_{2}} = 28/28 = 1\), \(n_{He} = 8/4 = 2\), \(n_{Ne} = 40/20 = 2\); total \(= 5\ \text{mol}\).\nMole fraction \(x_{N_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{5} = 0.2\).\nPartial pressure \(P_{N_{2}} = x_{N_{2}} \times P_{\text{total}} = 0.2 \times 20 = 4\ \text{bar}\).
61.note: Answer key says B (5 bar) which is WRONG. Mole fraction of N2 = 1/5 = 0.2, so partial pressure = 0.2 x 20 = 4 bar = option C. The AK even derives x = 1/5 then mis-states the product.

62.subtopic: Molecular Orbital Theory and Bond Order
62.solution: Counting electrons in bonding molecular orbitals: \(N_{2}\) has 10 bonding electrons and \(O_{2}\) also has 10 bonding electrons. They are equal, so the statement that \(N_{2}\) has MORE bonding electrons than \(O_{2}\) is incorrect. (\(O_{2}\) is less stable only because it has more antibonding electrons.) The other statements are correct: \(N_{2}\) is more stable than \(O_{2}\), its bond order is 3, and it is diamagnetic.

63.solution: Boiling points of hydrogen halides: HF is highest due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding (293 K). For the rest the boiling point rises with molecular size: HI (238 K) > HBr (206 K) > HCl (189 K). Overall: \(HF > HI > HBr > HCl\).

64.solution: Glucose \(C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}\) has 6 carbon atoms per molecule.\nCarbon atoms \(= 0.35 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 6 = 1.264 \times 10^{24}\).

65.subtopic: Van't Hoff Factor and Abnormal Molar Mass
65.solution: For the non-electrolyte: \(\Delta T_{b} = K_{b}\,m = x\ \text{K}\).\n\(AlCl_{3}\) dissociates: \(AlCl_{3} \to Al^{3+} + 3Cl^{-}\), giving 4 particles, so van't Hoff factor \(i = 4\).\nHence \(\Delta T_{b} = i \times K_{b}\,m = 4x\ \text{K}\).
65.note: Stem OCR garbled: 'ImAlCl3' = 1 m AlCl3 solution; 'delta T_6' = delta T_b.

66.subtopic: Batteries, Primary, Secondary and Fuel Cells
66.solution: In a dry (Leclanche) cell the positive electrode (cathode) is the site of reduction: \(2MnO_{2(s)} + 2NH_{4}^{+} + 2e^{-} \to Mn_{2}O_{3(s)} + 2NH_{3} + H_{2}O\). Thus \(MnO_{2}\) (Mn in +4) is reduced to \(Mn_{2}O_{3}\) (Mn in +3).

67.subtopic: pH, pOH and Ionic Product of Water

68.solution: The sum of oxidation numbers in a neutral compound is zero. Test \(X_{3}(YZ_{4})_{3}\): \(3(+3) + 3[(+5) + 4(-2)] = 9 + 3(-3) = 9 - 9 = 0\). It is the only formula that sums to zero.

69.subtopic: Group 2 Alkaline Earth Metals, Properties and Reactivity
69.solution: Quicklime is calcium oxide (CaO), obtained by thermal decomposition (calcination) of calcium carbonate: \(CaCO_{3} \xrightarrow{\Delta} CaO + CO_{2}\).

70.solution: The extent of adsorption increases with ease of liquefaction of the gas, i.e. with higher critical temperature. \(SO_{2}\) (critical temp ~430 K) has the highest critical temperature among the options and is adsorbed to the greatest extent.

71.solution: Silver nanoparticles act as a highly effective antibacterial disinfectant and are used to remove E. coli bacteria from water.

72.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
72.solution: The reaction \(NO_{2} + NO_{2} \to 2NO + O_{2}\) is an elementary reaction in which two \(NO_{2}\) molecules collide, so molecularity \(= 2\). For an elementary reaction the order equals the molecularity, so order \(= 2\).

73.note: Stem garbled: solubility reads 'x10^-4' but intended value is 4x10^-4 mol dm^-3 (only value consistent with keyed option B).

74.subtopic: Physical Properties of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
74.solution: All four options are isomeric butanols \((C_{4}H_{9}OH)\). Boiling point decreases with increased branching (more compact, smaller surface area, weaker van der Waals forces). The most branched isomer, 2-methylpropan-2-ol (tert-butanol, option D), has the lowest boiling point.

75.solution: In \(BrF_{5}\) the central Br has 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (\(sp^{3}d^{2}\), octahedral electron geometry). With one lone pair the molecular shape is square pyramidal.

76.solution: Cleavage of the \(C-X\) bond in haloarenes (aromatic nucleophilic substitution) is accelerated by electron-withdrawing \(-NO_{2}\) groups at the ortho/para positions. More \(-NO_{2}\) groups means greater reactivity. Compound III (2,4,6-trinitro) is most reactive, followed by the dinitro/nitro structures: \(III > II > I\).
76.note: Stem figures: (I) and (II) are p-nitrochlorobenzene type (mono/di-nitro chloroarene), (III) is 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene (picryl chloride, three -NO2). The two extracted images for I and II (image15, image16) appear nearly identical (both show Cl/para-NO2); reactivity order keyed by EWG count: III(3 NO2) > II > I. Answer D consistent.

77.solution: In the spectrochemical series the field strength increases as \(I^{-} < SCN^{-} < C_{2}O_{4}^{2-} < ... < CN^{-} < CO\). Among the options \(CN^{-}\) is the strongest field ligand.

79.solution: Polyacrylonitrile is prepared by addition polymerization of acrylonitrile, \(H_{2}C=CH-CN\).
79.stemOverride: Identify the monomer used in preparation of polyacrylonitrile.
79.note: Original option extraction was malformed (duplicate '(a)' labels, 1 image). Reconstructed: image18 shows isoprene H2C=C(CH3)-CH=CH2; options A=tetrafluoroethene, B=isoprene(image), C=acrylonitrile(answer), D=1,3-butadiene. Acrylonitrile is the monomer of polyacrylonitrile.

80.solution: Ethanal undergoes aldol condensation with dilute NaOH to give 3-hydroxybutanal (A). On heating (\(\Delta\)) this dehydrates to the alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde, B), \(CH_{3}-CH=CH-CHO\).

81.subtopic: Nucleic Acids, DNA, RNA, Nucleotides and Bases
81.solution: The pyrimidine ring of nucleic acid bases has two nitrogen atoms at positions 1 and 3 of the six-membered ring.

82.solution: The methoxy (\(-OCH_{3}\)) group is an activating, ortho/para-directing substituent. Bromination of anisole with \(Br_{2}\) in acetic acid (mild, monobromination) gives predominantly the para product, p-bromoanisole (the bulky ortho position is less favoured).

84.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
84.solution: Alkyl groups release electrons (+I effect), stabilizing the positive charge on the nitrogen of the protonated species. More alkyl groups means greater stabilization: \(NH_{4}^{+} < RNH_{3}^{+} < R_{2}NH_{2}^{+} < R_{3}NH^{+}\). The trialkyl-substituted cation \(R_{3}NH^{+}\) is most stable.

85.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life

86.solution: Tryptophan (Trp) is a neutral amino acid. Arginine (Arg) and lysine (Lys) are basic; glutamic acid (Glu) is acidic.

87.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
87.solution: Nernst equation: \(E_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log_{10}\dfrac{[Cd^{2+}]}{[Cu^{2+}]}\).\nWith \([Cd^{2+}] = 10[Cu^{2+}]\): \(E_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log_{10}10 = E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} - 0.0296\ \text{V}\).\nSo \(E_{\text{cell}}\) is less than \(E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}\) by 0.0296 V.

88.solution: Dacron (Terylene, a polyester) blended with cotton gives the wrinkle-free fabric terycot.

89.solution: A secondary amine has two carbon (alkyl/aryl) groups attached to nitrogen. N-Methylethanamine, \(CH_{3}-NH-CH_{2}CH_{3}\), has two alkyl groups on N and is a secondary amine. Ethane-1,2-diamine and propan-2-amine are primary.

90.subtopic: Colour, Magnetic Properties and Spin-Only Formula
90.solution: Magnetic moment \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\) increases with the number of unpaired electrons. \(Cu^{2+}\) is \(3d^{9}\) (1 unpaired, \(\mu = 1.73\) BM); \(Cr^{3+}\ 3d^{3}\) and \(Co^{2+}\ 3d^{7}\) have 3 unpaired; \(Fe^{2+}\ 3d^{6}\) has 4 unpaired. \(Cu^{2+}\) has the least magnetic moment.

91.subtopic: IUPAC Nomenclature, Functional Groups and Homologous Series
91.solution: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) contains an ESTER linkage (and a carboxylic acid group), not an amide linkage. So the statement 'It contains amide linkage' is false. The other statements (obtained from salicylic acid, fewer side effects than salicylic acid, stomach-irritating) are true.

92.subtopic: Nomenclature and Classification of Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
92.solution: Boiling point of aldehydes increases with molecular weight (stronger van der Waals forces). Valeraldehyde (pentanal, \(C_{4}H_{9}CHO\)) is the largest and has the highest boiling point.

93.subtopic: Crystal Defects, Magnetic Properties and Semiconductors
93.solution: An n-type semiconductor is formed by doping a Group 14 element (Ge) with a Group 15 element that has an extra valence electron. Among the options, arsenic (As) is the Group 15 dopant; B, In and Ga are Group 13 (p-type dopants).
93.note: Classified under Semiconductor Devices (a Physics chapter) because the MHT-CET Chemistry taxonomy has no semiconductor-doping subtopic; this is the closest fit. (Chemistry's Solid State 'Crystal Defects, Magnetic Properties and Semiconductors' is an alternative.)

94.solution: Entropy decreases when randomness decreases, i.e. when going from a more disordered to a more ordered state. Condensation of a gas to a liquid, \(H_{2}O_{(g)} \to H_{2}O_{(l)}\), decreases entropy. The other options (solid to liquid/gas, liquid to gas) all increase entropy.

95.solution: The statement that no two electrons in an atom can have an identical set of four quantum numbers is Pauli's exclusion principle.

96.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
96.solution: Diborane \((B_{2}H_{6})\) selectively reduces the carboxylic acid group \(-COOH\) to a primary alcohol. It does not reduce esters \((-COOR)\), nitro groups \((-NO_{2})\) or halides \((-X)\) under the same conditions.

97.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
97.solution: The structure (image) is a cyclopentane ring bearing an \(-OH\) on C1 and methyl groups on the two carbons adjacent to it (C2 and C5). The IUPAC name is 2,5-dimethylcyclopentanol (C1 carrying OH gets locant 1, the two methyls at 2 and 5).
97.note: Stem figure (image19): cyclopentanol ring with OH on C1 and CH3 on the two adjacent ring carbons (C2 and C5). Options B and D (open-chain pentanol / 'cyclopentan-2-ol') are wrong since the parent is a cyclopentanol where the OH-bearing carbon is C1.

98.solution: The product is 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid), formed by warming the substrate with water. This hydrolysis (aromatic nucleophilic substitution of Cl by OH) occurs readily only when three strongly activating \(-NO_{2}\) groups are present ortho/para to the halogen. Hence the substrate S is 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene (picryl chloride).
98.note: Stem figure (image20): S + warm H2O -> 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid). Substrate must be 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene.

99.subtopic: Reactions of Alkenes, Addition, Oxidation and Ozonolysis
99.solution: Hydroboration-oxidation of propene proceeds with anti-Markovnikov regiochemistry: \(B\) and \(H\) add across the double bond with B at the terminal (less substituted) carbon, and alkaline \(H_{2}O_{2}\) replaces B with OH. The product is the primary alcohol propan-1-ol.

100.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy
